ATT-03.source_class: Elsevier/Neuron original official article associated supplemental data CDN
ATT-03.verified_structure: Original publication ID Neuron 61:168-185 2009 and titled 'The Normalization Model of Attention'; additional derivations for main Figs4C,4E,5C,6C,7C, supplied equations [S1]-[S16]
verified_conditional_findings: Fig4C nonpreferred direction attention increases fixed additive suppressive term; contrast gain shifts according to sigma prime versus sigma double-prime (supplement pp2-3)

Fig4E shared stimulus contrast and differing preferred/nonpreferred attention give low-contrast gain gamma and high-contrast saturated response gain; approximation-dependent (supplement p3 [S5]-[S10])
Fig5C orientation-uniform attention and suppression pooling yield separable contrast response and tuning [S11]-[S12] (supplement p3-4)
Fig6C feature-focused attention multiplies feature tuning [S13] when suppressive convolution approximately constant across motion directions (supplement p4)
Fig7C three attentional conditions [S14]-[S16] predict asymmetric elevation and sharpening only if nonflat attention field (supplement p4-5)
adverse: All S3-S16 results are stated conditional approximations (flat/broad suppressive field, fixed nonpreferred contrast, high/low contrast); not universal exact full biophysical proof
No new numerical author-model replay or independent empirical dataset reproduction claimed
ATT-03.remaining: Original paper whole numeric fitting/biophysical mechanisms and global ancestry separately held

BLF-01.source_class: Europe PMC official archive package supplementaryFiles zip member mmc1.pdf; publicly OA published article-associated supplemental Figure S1
BLF-01.verified_structure: iScience volume28 supplemental Figure S1, Exp S manipulating short 2s versus long 8s ITI, reported separately by granularity G=2 and G=8 in choice and stimulus history regressions
verified_conditional_findings: Figure S1 pp2 supports publisher main text p19: granularity effect is not weakened with long ITI, contrary to classic choice hysteresis explanation; main reports stronger long-ITI effect

Figure S1's Exp S diverged methodologically from Exp1-7: MRI task, 7T scanner, broader uncalibrated disk-size distribution, extreme 28% of stimulus distribution excluded. This prevents unqualified generalization across experimental procedures.
adverse: Small main-reported supplementary participant sample 16; confidence and absolute coefficients not independently re-fit from raw participants
Figure S1 only; this supplement contains no additional entire original model proof or fixes main prose's 12/16 or 3/4-count inconsistencies
BLF-01.remaining: Main experimental quantitative coefficient inventory and generalization limits remain source-science conditional

Supplement p3 eq(4)-(5) specifies TD learning algorithms for SR and PR, with switched target current predecessor state-action for PR.
